independence_note: Read only the review brief, rubric, workflow, relevant blueprint/config and this blind four-dialogue source. No expected-results file, authored batch, notes, questions, options, keys or other review was opened.

items.situation_summary: Daan notices Roos dancing with a broom and asks about turning music on. The replies shift to instrument choices and then to furniture and tableware.
items.communicative_purpose: Starting music is the stated request. The exchange never establishes why preparing chairs, plates or glasses helps with that request.
items.contrivance_check: Fails. Radio, guitar and piano are presented as interchangeable ways to turn music on without establishing a performance. The later stock of chairs, plates and glasses serves no stated interaction.
unsupported_assumptions: A live performance would make the guitar and piano relevant alternatives to turning on a radio.
An unstated gathering would connect chairs, plates and glasses to the music request.
reasons: The reply changes the object category from switching on music to choosing between a device and instruments.
The final two turns add unrelated stocktaking instead of completing the music exchange.
items.repair_scope: Replace the dialogue premise or develop a new, explicitly linked exchange. A literal quoted answer would not repair the source.

items.situation_summary: Roos wants to find her pen. Ruben first locates her book and telephone, then answers her direct question about the pen.
items.communicative_purpose: Helping Roos find her pen is clear, and the final answer achieves it. Ruben’s first reply does not help with that search as written.
items.contrivance_check: Fails locally. The book and telephone are a pair of unrelated location facts. The source gives no reason to inventory them when Roos asks for her pen.
unsupported_assumptions: The book or telephone would provide a useful clue to the pen’s location, although the dialogue never supplies that connection.
reasons: The second turn responds to a search for a pen by naming other objects.
The third and fourth turns are coherent, so replacing the unrelated second turn can repair the exchange.
items.repair_scope: Replace the second turn with a direct contribution to the pen search. Do not add an off-page explanation for the other objects.

items.situation_summary: A waiter takes a customer’s soup order and asks whether the customer also wants bread.
items.communicative_purpose: The exchange establishes the soup choice and whether to serve bread.
items.contrivance_check: Passes. The list names real alternatives the customer must choose between. Bread is a relevant follow-up to the soup order.
reasons: Each reply answers the preceding service question.
The choices and follow-up both serve the order rather than supplying unrelated distractor facts.

items.situation_summary: A notices B wearing a pan on their head. B explains that their hat is wet, asks to borrow A’s coat and then says they can go outside.
items.communicative_purpose: B explains the visible oddity and obtains permission and a location for the coat needed to go outside.
items.contrivance_check: Passes. The wet hat supplies an explicit reason for the pan. The coat request is followed by permission, its location and the stated next action.
reasons: The unusual object is grounded by the wet-hat explanation.
The request, permission and thanks form a coherent practical exchange.
